_comment: Defaults of the correctness gate. Every value can be overridden by a flag (--gate, --gate-tolerance, ...). The tolerance default mirrors pz's own `quality-tolerance` setting (src/config/pz_config.c); keep them equal. The text is a frozen copy so perplexity numbers stay comparable between runs (sha256 is recorded in every gate.json).
_clean_note: A pz binary whose version ends in -dirty is a build of uncommitted state that cannot be reproduced (docs/rca: the first published sweep ran int4 at 26.5 tok/s with one; clean builds give about 20). Timed runs refuse it unless --allow-dirty-binary.
_time_note: A cell that fails the gate (INVALID) is neither timed nor screenshotted in strict mode: a speed for a wrong computation means nothing. Its verdict stays in gate.json and the summary lists it as not timed. Set true to time it anyway.

approximate._comment: Variants that are lossy by design (a documented speed/accuracy trade the user chooses). They are judged APPROX: shown with the measured gap, never excluded. Add `tolerance_pct` to an entry to make it a hard bound.

pz-auto-fast.why: --classifier auto-fast: picks the fastest LM-head precision

ppl_regex: Final estimate: PPL(?: over \d+ chunks for n_ctx=\d+)? = ([0-9.]+)

verdicts.INVALID: outside warn_factor x tolerance, or the smoke answer is wrong
verdicts.UNVERIFIED: no reference result to compare with
verdicts.REF: the reference itself (must pass the smoke check)
verdicts.APPROX: lossy by design (config `approximate`); the gap to the reference is reported, not judged
